CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female with quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. Patient was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021 and discharged on 07/02/2021. She presented with increasing concerns for spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. In the emergency department she was febrile with white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for urinary tract infection and she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. She slowly improved and was discharged after clinical improvement. She has a supra-pubic catheter. Patient believes her hospitalization was more likely related to severe constipation and dysreflexia causing blood pressure elevation rather than a true urinary tract infection. She notes that urine cultures obtained were not very impressive. She reports feeling significantly better after having a bowel movement at home. She went to the hospital because her blood pressure was out of control, causing headache and vomiting. She now feels back to her normal self. Doctor attributes some of the illness to the extremely hot weather during late June, which can lead to dehydration and worsen constipation. Patient reports she tends to stay inside more during hot weather.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current pain or discomfort anywhere. Denies current spasms or lightheadedness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury
Constipation
Supra-pubic catheter

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily; doubles when bowel movements are infrequent
Lactulose as rescue treatment for severe constipation
Vitamin C
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Stays indoors more during hot weather but does go out occasionally. Unvaccinated for COVID. Concerned about vaccine side effects and reports of vaccine injury. Does not receive annual flu shot. Takes supplements. Describes self as somewhat homeopathic.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal breathing
General: No acute distress
Pain: Denies pain or discomfort

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization (06/29-07/02/2021):
White blood cell count 23,000 (elevated)
Urine cultures obtained but not very impressive
Prior year WBC was normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute to chronic constipation: Believes recent hospitalization was related to constipation and dysreflexia rather than true UTI. Continue current bowel regimen with miralax as primary treatment and lactulose for rescue. Discussed contribution of dehydration during hot weather to constipation.

2. Leukocytosis: Return in 2-3 weeks for fasting labs including CBC to recheck white blood cell count and cholesterol panel. Will monitor if WBC normalizes; if it remains elevated, this would suggest other bowel pathology.

3. Quadriplegia: Stable

4. COVID-19 vaccine: Patient currently unvaccinated and hesitant about vaccine. Discussed vaccine safety, side effects, and concerns about vaccine injury. Doctor strongly recommends vaccination given high-risk status from quadriplegia. Discussed that supplements are not adequate preventative. Doctor expressed concern if she does not get vaccinated. Patient is somewhat open-minded and will consider vaccine.
